title: Enterprise supplier portal
subtitle: Modernized frontend for a multi-service supplier platform
overview: I led the frontend work for a supplier portal used across many teams. We consolidated scattered React apps written in JavaScript into a single TypeScript codebase, improved developer workflows, and made the UI more predictable for users and integrators.
challenge: The portal had grown organically in dozens of repositories. Different teams copied similar code, patterns diverged, and TypeScript coverage was low. That made changes slow, introduced bugs, and made on-boarding new developers harder.
solution: We moved to a centralized frontend architecture using React + TypeScript and a shared component library. I introduced consistent patterns for state and API integration, set up incremental migration paths so services could move at their own pace, and added tests and automation to reduce regressions.

keyAchievements.title: Shared component library
keyAchievements.description: Built a small, well-documented component library that replaced duplicated UI code and made interfaces consistent across services.

keyAchievements.title: Incremental migration
keyAchievements.description: Migrated services gradually to TypeScript and the new architecture to avoid big-bang rewrites and reduce downtime.

keyAchievements.title: Developer experience
keyAchievements.description: Standardized linting, CI checks, and local dev tooling so onboarding and day-to-day work are faster and less error-prone.

keyAchievements.title: Service abstraction
keyAchievements.description: Created clear API integration layers so frontend teams can work with multiple backend services without repeating business logic.

keyAchievements.title: Performance work
keyAchievements.description: Reduced bundle size, added code-splitting and lazy loading in key areas to improve perceived page speed.

learnings: TypeScript reduces a lot of wasted time — not a magic fix, but it helps.
Small shared components plus clear docs beats large UI frameworks for maintenance.
Incremental migration keeps the business running while the code improves.
Designing APIs with frontends in mind makes orchestration far simpler.
